coverage_note: Latin-transliterated stretch from ~[13:33] to ~[24:35] and again ~[27:17]-[31:40], [38:14]-[40:46], [42:30]-[48:13], [50:40]-[1:01:44]; many Medi turns are only '[speaking Arabic]' / '[speaking foreign language]' ([03:25], [04:22], [05:28], [06:13], [06:28], [26:46]-[27:45], [28:26]-[28:55], [29:56]-[31:27], [1:02:48]-[1:03:27], [1:04:29]-[1:05:47], [1:07:09]-[1:08:21], [1:09:06]) so several of her fixes there are filed low-confidence with his line unseen. English-only stretch [40:53]-[42:10] (groove chat). Pronunciation-only slips NOT filed (S4): ح->ه throughout the 7ammas drill (بيهمسوني/بيحمسوني etc.), ض->د in daaya2, dropped ع (amalti, daya), بحسب for بعصب [11:30], بتسكر for بتذكر [10:31], بندارة for kundara [08:32], فيسة for تسعة [07:41], the long-vowel fixes دايقني [44:52] and تدايقي [51:16], 'It's a three' [30:08]. Self-fixes not filed: ستطاش->ستاش, خلت->ربع [07:53], بنوجع->بنتوجع [37:38], daya una->tedaya u minna [52:52], baharrak->bit haraki [1:01:33]. [24:50] 'shway batit' unreadable. Chat lines used as fix signals where her voice said nothing (signal chat-fix).

rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: 'I should have taught her' needs kaan stacked on laazem plus a bare present verb; he gave laazem alone with a past-tense verb, she recast the whole clause and glossed it 'I should have / I had to'.
rows.english: I should have taught her everything

rows.why: He offered the get-form ta3allam (sheet: learn | et3allam) for 'teach'; the make-form is 3allem (sheet: teach | 3allem), which is what she recast.

rows.chat: heye z8eere kteer u ma ba3ref keef heyye ra7 teshte8el
rows.why: His Arabic is untranscribed; she prompted the first letter then supplied the word (sheet: small | Z8eer), so filed as a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: If I say, if I say [speaking Arabic] , it wouldn't make sense?
rows.amal_said: أنا لازم تصير؟ No. You'd need something like to make her، to make to let her become.
rows.chat: bas ana ra7 ajrreb a5alliha t9eer muwazzafe mnee7a
rows.why: 'Make her become' needs the causative a5alliha (let/make her) before tseer; 'ana laazem tseer' pairs an I-subject with a she-verb and has no make/let verb, and she said No outright.
rows.english: I'll try to make her become a good employee

rows.medi_said: make her a good [speaking Arabic] Would it be [speaking Arabic] ?
rows.why: He asked 'would it be ...?' and she supplied موظفة (sheet: employee | Muwazzaf); his attempt is untranscribed so it cannot be scored as wrong.
'One more' is kamaan wa7ad (sheet: also / more / too | Kamaan; one more time | Kaman marra); aktar is the comparative 'more than', so wa7ad aktar is an English calque she recast at once.
Repeat of 0916-6 one minute later; she recast to كمان واحد again and he echoed 'دول واحد' (ضل واحد).

rows.medi_said: this a T? بنسـ-- بنسوار أو بسوار؟
rows.why: He guessed an n- prefix pair (banSawwar) for the photograph verb; she said No and later 'the only one that was an was بكسر، بانكسر', i.e. this pair is bSawwer / btSawwar. Asked as a meta question, so low.

rows.medi_said: to behamasu ki-- / uh, past tense.
rows.amal_said: No، it's present، بس it's one، not group of things. / شو بيحمسك؟
rows.why: 'What excites you' has a singular subject (shu = it); he used the they-form bey7ammsu + ki and called it past; she said No, present, one thing, then said the sentence.

rows.amal_said: Made. / Past. He made me excited.
rows.why: He answered a past prompt with the present bey7ammesni; she prompted 'Made. Past.' and he produced hamasni, which she accepted.

rows.amal_said: It's the wrong verb. It's get excited, not excite.
rows.why: Command 'get excited' is the get-form t7ammasi; he gave the make-form 7ammsi (excite me/someone) and she named it the wrong verb.

rows.medi_said: Oh, you're right. Okay. Uh, tetamasi.
rows.why: The get-form command already starts with t- (t7ammasi); he stacked a second te- as if adding a you-prefix; she said 'No T, just one T' and he fixed to tamasi.

rows.amal_said: This is why don't you get excited? ... we are using the adjective here because it's are. You are excited.
rows.why: 'Why aren't you excited (now)' takes the participle mit7ammse with mish, not the habitual verb ma bti7ammasi; she explained the adjective and he produced 'Lesh mish mithamsa' at [18:27].
'We got excited' is the get-form t7ammasna; the engine has him saying 7ammasna (we excited someone); she said Mm-hmm aloud but typed t7ammasna. Could be a dropped t in transcription.
rows.english: We got excited on the road.

rows.amal_said: street. What's the road? / Like the way on the road.
rows.why: Prompt was 'on the road'; he said shaare3 (sheet: street | Shaare3) and she prompted 'street. What's the road?' until he gave 3ala el taree- (sheet: road / way / route | 6ariq).

rows.medi_said: Or ala el shara? No, fi el shara.
rows.why: He weighed fi against 3ala and settled on fi ('in the street'); 'on the road' takes 3ala, which he switched to himself once the noun changed and which her chat confirms.

rows.amal_said: الـ safar. Safra is one trip. Safar is...
rows.why: 'Traveling' as a noun is safar (sheet: traveling (noun) | Safar); safra is one trip (sheet: (travel) trip | Safra); she recast and explained the difference.
'Excite me more' needs the object -ni on the command; he left it off, she prompted 'Me' and he produced hamasini akthar.

rows.medi_said: They got too excited. Humma ziyada.
rows.amal_said: Let's put it at the after.
rows.why: He fronted the adverb ziyaade before the verb; she moved it to the end and he rebuilt 'ta hamasu ziyada'.
kaan must carry the I-ending (kunt) for 'I was / used to work'; he used bare kaan (he-form) and she recast 'kunt', which he took up.

rows.medi_said: Ana kunnet ashtagil bi il AI
rows.why: He said bi for 'in (a field)'; her chat has fi; nothing said aloud and bi/fi overlap in Levantine, so low.
Object 'you (f)' on a verb is -ki; he tried -ik then -nek; she recast afarjiki and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: We, we need to learn this verb نكمل. Continue. / أنا بكمل as I continue
rows.why: Didn't-know: she introduced kammal = continue (vs kaamel = whole) and he had not attempted it; he then asked whether it means 'in total'.

rows.medi_said: [speaking foreign language] I hurt. [speaking foreign language] I hurt someone. [speaking foreign language] I hurt. I get hurt.
rows.amal_said: Bilaks. Bawajja' is I hurt someone, and batwajja' is I am the one being hurt. I get hurt.
rows.right: bawajje3 = I hurt someone; batwajja3 = I get hurt
rows.why: Asked which of bawajje3/batwajja3 means what, he glossed them backwards; she said 'Bilaks' (the opposite) and gave the pairing. His Arabic is untranscribed, only his English glosses show the swap.
rows.english: I hurt someone / I get hurt

rows.medi_said: uh, [speaking foreign language] is... Hold on. How do-- I don't know if it's like to...
rows.why: He stalled ('I don't know if it's like to...') and she supplied the form; 'It's a three' suggests he also said 2 for 3, which is pronunciation.
ijr is feminine so the verb is btwajje3; he used the masculine bywajje3, she said '(leg) is feminine' and he produced بتوجع at [32:45].
Told the noun is feminine, he changed the owner ending to -ak instead of fixing the verb; she said No and he went back to رجله.
Sheet: leg / foot | Ejer (F) | إجر; he used رجل (rijl); she let it pass aloud and typed ijro; he uses ijrik himself at [1:01:42], so this may be a slip rather than a gap.
Subject is ana, so the verb is ba-wajj3ek; he used the he-form bey-wajj3ek; she said nothing aloud but typed bawajj3ek.

rows.amal_said: is did I hurt you? Did you get hurt?
rows.why: 'Did you get hurt' is the intransitive t-form with the you-ending -ti; he hung an object -ek on it, which she read back as 'did I hurt you?'; he then fixed to تواجاتي.

rows.amal_said: No, by me. / Because of me.
rows.why: 'By / because of me' rides on the preposition min (minni); he attached an object -ni to the get-hurt verb; she said No and he reached تواجهتي مني at [36:53].
rows.english: Did you get hurt by me?

rows.why: 'Don't hurt her' is the make-form twajj3i + ha; he used the get-form titwajja3i with an object; she repeated the prompt and he rebuilt it.
Negative command is ma + the YOU-form (t-); he dropped the t- prefix; she said 'Very close' and he produced Ma tiwajaiha, which she accepted.

rows.medi_said: ana tawajet, tawaja'et, tawaja'et min shu haketni.
rows.why: 7aka takes la- for the person told (7akait-li); he attached a direct -ni; she said ممتاز aloud but typed 7akkaitili.
rows.english: I got hurt by what you told me.

rows.medi_said: bidayai, bidayi. Is it bidayayi or bidayi?
rows.amal_said: So what upsets you? So the what is the he, and then upsets you.
rows.why: 'What upsets you' = he-form + object -ek; his forms had no object and a you/I prefix; she spelled out 'the what is the he, then upsets you' and he produced shu bitaiek.

rows.medi_said: daya u-- daya u ni. Daya u ni.
rows.why: Object 'you (f)' is -ki; he put -ni (me); she prompted 'You' and he fixed to daya u ki.

After illi the verb grows the pointer -ih (3melt-ih); her chat has it, his line lacks it; her spoken 'عملت' may only be the dropped ع, and when he repeated 'ili amalti' at [50:44] she said ممتاز, so low.

rows.amal_said: كان بيضايق not ت 'cause it makes people upset. It upsets.
rows.why: 'Was upsetting' = it upsets = make-form daaye2; he used the get-form etdaaya2 and she said 'not ت'; he then pointed out kaan drops the b- and she agreed (كان يضايق).
Subject is 'they'; he started with huwe (he); she prompted 'They' and he switched to hume. Pronoun rather than verb, filed under subject agreement for want of a pronoun bucket.
rows.english: I suppose they got upset with us.

rows.why: The object -ha on shuft came out as -a; she recast شفتها; may be only a dropped h (pronunciation), so low.
'Last week' is el-usboo3 el-maadi; the engine wrote 'avadi' (possibly 3aadi = ordinary, or a mangled maadi) and he repeated 'Ashu avadi' after her recast; wording unverifiable so low.

rows.amal_said: ما عنده عكس. / بس hacks on its own is like the noun for opposite.
rows.why: Sheet: opposite (bel-3aks = on the contrary) | 3aks; he used the adverb bil-3aks as the noun 'an opposite'; she recast ما عنده عكس and explained the two uses.

rows.medi_said: Uh, haraki halak. [laughs] Uh, there's an or?
rows.why: Telling a woman to move herself, he used the feminine verb 7arraki with the masculine -ak on 7aal; her chat has 7aalek; her spoken 'حرك حالك' is unvowelled so low.
Sheet: bed | Ta5t; the engine heard akhti (my sister) for 'my bed'; she said Mm aloud and typed ta5ti; likely a dropped t in transcription, so low.
rows.english: I moved my bed to the right.

rows.amal_said: La el yameen. / Bas ana baharrek something la el yameen.
rows.why: Moving something TO a side takes la (lal-yameen); 3ala is for directions you give (rou7 3ala el-yameen) - note her sheet lists 'to the right | 3ala el-yameen' for that use; she recast and explained at length.
rows.english: I moved my bed to the right.

rows.medi_said: so move yourself to the left. Uh, taharki ila shmal.
rows.why: He used MSA ila and dropped el- right after the la-vs-3ala discussion; she said Mm-hmm aloud but typed lal-shmaal (la + el-).

rows.amal_said: Ashya ak or ashya ek. Ashya e.
rows.why: 'Your things' - he did not have the plural ashyaa2 (sheet has only thing | Eshi) and said 'I don't think we've used that before'; she supplied it.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] Two is ala? / [speaking Arabic] What's that?
rows.why: She recast the demonstrative + table (هذي الطاولة), which points at a wrong hada/hadi or article on his side; his line is untranscribed so low.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] Two is ala? / Uh, so is it alawain?
rows.amal_said: It's لوين. / يا لوين. From to is la.
rows.why: Didn't-know: 'to where' is la-wain; he asked whether 'to' is 3ala and said 'I don't think I've ever said this before'; also C10 (preposition fronted onto the question word).
rows.english: Where will you move this table to?

rows.amal_said: ورقة is feminine and one. ورق is plural. / ورقة حركت أنت.
rows.why: 'The papers' is the collective wara2 with a plural verb (t7arraku); he used the singular wara2a (sheet: leaf / paper / sheet | Waraqa) and she named the singular/plural rule before he rebuilt it.
rows.english: The papers moved from the wind.

rows.chat: lamma 3indna zabaayen u bidna nfarjihom el-sajjad
rows.why: 'When we have customers' = 3indna; he said 3indhom (they have); she recast عندنا and, asked 'What'd I say?', told him عندهم.

rows.medi_said: nifarijini or nifarj-? It's nifariji, nifariji.
rows.why: 'Show them' needs the object -hom on nfarji; he settled on bare nfarji (after trying -ni); she recast فرجيهم.
rows.english: we want to show them the carpets

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] [laughs] Does that, [laughs] does that not work?
rows.amal_said: الله يعافيكي بس. / أو الله يعافيكي ألف مرة or I don't know.
rows.right: الله يعافيكي (بس) / الله يعافيكي ألف مرة
rows.why: He built a reply to يعطيك ألف عافية (untranscribed, apparently echoing ألف); she gave the set replies; a fixed-expression fix, low because his words are unseen.
rows.english: reply to 'may God give you a thousand strengths'

rows.why: 'What did you get upset about' is the get-form etdaaya2ti; the engine has daaya2ti (you upset); she said Yes; chat has the t-form; may be transcription, so low.
rows.english: What did you get upset about?
